messages.subject: Greetings and Seeking Shiny Expertise
messages.subject_clean: Greetings and Seeking Shiny Expertise
messages.body_plain:
Happy New Year!

I have developed an app (in collaboration) devoted to analyzing course gradebook data. The goal is to provide an easy tool that enables instructors to produce summary statistics and plots to visualize student performance. The app is currently hosted here: http://gradebook.plb.ucdavis.edu:8080/. It is built using React (www.reactjs.org <http://www.reactjs.org>) and uses a separate server running R. The plots are built using Plotly.

The programmer I have been working with is very busy and unable to continue development. There are several changes I would like to make, but I am curious to know the feasibility of re-building it as a Shiny app. I would be grateful for opinions from Shiny enthusiasts.

I am also open to hiring a GSR or similar position to bring this project to fruition. If you have experience working in React or think you could develop this into a Shiny app, please contact me (jmle...@ucdavis.edu).

Thank you!

messages.subject: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
messages.subject_clean: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I have a long vector of numbers x and a vector Cats denoting which category each number belongs to. I'd like to aggregate x by Cats in base R, and was thinking of using lapply. Is there a fast way to create a list where elements of x belonging to different Cats would be in different list entries?

Example: x=1:10, Cats=rep(1:3,c(3,3,4)), and the resulting list looks like x.list=list(rep(1,3),rep(2,3),rep(3,4)). Then I could do lapply(x.list,sum).

Would love to hear alternative suggestions; my only preference is for base R and speed (I'll need to aggregate 10,000-long vectors billions of times).

Many thanks and happy new year!

messages.body_plain:
Don't know about the speed, but here's a base-R solution, using the
"by" function (which is a wrapper for the "tapply" function).
Bottom line:

> lapply(x.list,sum)  ## from the statement of the problem

[[1]]
[1] 3

[[2]]
[1] 6

[[3]]
[1] 12

> sums_list  ## from the proposed solution
$`1`
[1] 3

$`2`
[1] 6

$`3`
[1] 12

## Original example

x <- 1:10
x

Cats <- rep(1:3,c(3,3,4))
Cats

x.list <- list(rep(1,3),rep(2,3),rep(3,4))
x.list

lapply(x.list,sum)

## Possible solution

df <- data.frame(cbind(x, Cats))
df

sums_by <- by(df, df["Cats"], function(grp) {
    sum(grp["Cats"])
})
sums_by  ## object of class "by"

sums_list <- as.list(sums_by)
sums_list  ## object of class "list"

messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: append to list by factor / fast aggregation
messages.body_plain:
If I’m understanding you right, you can use split() to do this:

x.list = split(x, Cats)
lapply(x.list,sum)

I guessed that using tapply() directly would be fastest, but it appears the split() then lapply() is faster!

Did you mean for your sum() operation to not involve the x vector at all? Right now, your result suggests that you want to sum the numbers corresponding to the category labels. That is, x.list is the same as Cats but just diced up a little differently. If this is what you want, then use the split() function with Cats as both arguments (split(Cats, Cats))

library(microbenchmark)

x=1:10
Cats = rep(1:3,c(3,3,4))

microbenchmark(aggregate = aggregate(x, list(Cats), FUN = sum),
               tapply = tapply(X = x, INDEX = Cats, FUN = sum),
               hannon = { df <- data.frame(cbind(x, Cats))
                          sums_by <- by(df, df["Cats"], function(grp) {
                            sum(grp["Cats"])
                          })
                          sums_list <- as.list(sums_by)
                        },
               hannon_stay_as_by = { df <- data.frame(cbind(x, Cats))
               sums_by <- by(df, df["Cats"], function(grp) {
                 sum(grp["Cats"])
               })
               },
               split = {  x.list = split(x, Cats)
                          lapply(x.list,sum)}
               )
## Unit: microseconds
##               expr     min       lq       mean    median        uq
##          aggregate 576.872 603.2775  710.40752  624.3805  689.9060
##             tapply  79.339  93.8830  112.41990  104.1095  115.8365
##             hannon 571.793 597.6665 1513.54809  870.8985 1777.5830
##  hannon_stay_as_by 569.428 585.4495 1303.66409 1263.2130 1757.3600
##              split  52.606  64.0900   72.45376   71.8240   76.9565
##        max neval cld
##   2833.339   100  b
##    365.627   100 a
##  17538.522   100   c
##   4344.227   100   c
##    117.059   100 a

Maybe there’s an even faster way though?

x=1:10
Cats=rep(1:3,c(3,3,4))
df.cats = data.frame(X= x,  Cats=Cats) # create data frame
df.cats$Cats = as.factor(df.cats$Cats) # turn Cats  into a factor
nlevel = length(levels(df.cats$Cats)) # count how many levels you have
vecAggregate = vector(length = nlevel) # declare aggregate  vector of nlevel
for (i in 1:nlevel){
  df1 = subset(df.cats, Cats==i) # use subset function to extract information at each level
  vecAggregate[i] = sum(df1[,1]) # aggregate at each level
}

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we will be having a Meet and Analyze Data session from 3:00pm-5:00pm
today (01/09),
in the 1013 Valley Hall room (http://campusmap.ucdavis.edu/?b=178).
Hope to see you there!

--

If you think you are going to join us, please let us know --

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeUW5QS55uDwDpusGYerY542D_tQubkmPMtUKlGdbmoSWfSSQ/viewform

--

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message

messages.subject: D-RUG: Upcoming talks/presentations
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG: Upcoming talks/presentations
messages.body_plain:
Hi R folks!

Just wanted to let you know we'll be having a couple talks in the next month or so during our D-RUG meetings (Tues 12-2pm in DSI 360). Please come join us, ask questions, etc. Typically we will still have time after the talks for our usual work-session.

So coming up:
1/22 (Next week!): Reproducible Examples (REPREX) with Taylor Reiter
Given the many questions that get posed on our list-serv, as well as on StackOverflow or other discussion boards, it seemed a good time to have a short talk on what a reprex <https://reprex.tidyverse.org/articles/reprex-dos-and-donts.html> consists of, how to quickly generate a reprex, and why reprex are really key for getting questions answered.
2/12 Using the aggiedown <https://github.com/ryanpeek/aggiedown> package for writing your Dissertation with Ryan Peek
Writing your dissertation is hard...formatting it is even harder. If you are interested in using a bookdown/Rmarkdown template that has been formatted for UC Davis specifications to generate a clean and correctly typeset pdf of your work, please come ask questions or help me break this package so I can make it better.
As always, please feel free to come with questions/concerns or just some quiet coding time during our weekly worksessions.

Hope to see you next week.

Adios,
R

--

"When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the universe."
John Muir (My First Summer in the Sierra, 1911)
-----------------------------------------------------
Ryan Peek, PhD
Ecologist
Center for Watershed Sciences, UC Davis
ryanpeek.github.io <http://ryanpeek.github.io>
@riverpeek
530.754.5351

-----------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Get list of entries from a specific clade of a phylogenetic tree (Newick file)?
messages.subject_clean: Get list of entries from a specific clade of a phylogenetic tree (Newick file)?
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUG,

I'm building phylogenetic trees from fasta files of Rubisco protein sequences. Once the tree is made (I've been using mafft --> fastTree --> Newick file --> iToL), I can see which Rubsico sequences are Form I, which are Form II, etc, based on their phylogenetic grouping; all form I Rubisco are in one clade, etc.

I want to be able to get the list of form I entries, and separately the list of Form II entries, etc.

Seems very simple but haven't gotten much headway from SO / BioStars forums / fastTree documentation.

Thanks for any suggestions you might have!

Best,
Rey

messages.body_plain:
Hi D-Ruggies,

Just a quick note, we've updated the D-RUG website, and it now includes the screencast of Taylor's presentation on reprex <http://d-rug.github.io/blog/2019/Taylor-Reiter-reproducible-examples> (reproducible examples). Take a look if you missed it! There are some good points and discussion to consider as you think about posting/asking a question.

Next week (Tues Feb 5) I'll be giving a little demo of the aggiedown package <https://github.com/ryanpeek/aggiedown>, and how you might use it to write your dissertation/thesis (or a manuscript) in Rmarkdown, which can then be rendered to a lovely well formatted pdf. Mainly if you are interested in learning more about what you can do with Rmarkdown, bookdown <https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/>, come check it out. We'll screen cast as usual.

Thanks and happy coding,

Adios,
Ryan

--
